rationale: A wins because it gives the founder four real press lanes, not three envelopes around the same sustainability announcement. "Patagonia is building reverse logistics for clothing at national scale" is a specific operations-trade story; B's "Patagonia opens free repairs at every US store" is mostly the announcement with better manners. B has one strong skeptical line in "The retailer that won't say how much money its sustainability story makes," but it overlaps with its own data angle and then wanders into an invented resale expansion.
gaps_in_A: "Only a company with no shareholders to please could give repairs away" overstates the supplied ownership fact. Privately held and profit-directed-to-causes is relevant; "only" needs proof.
"triages it into free/at-cost/resale" assumes a repair-intake-to-resale routing that the update does not actually give.
"The prevailing model in apparel is volume" is a useful business frame, but it needs outside support before it becomes pitch copy.
"national scale" is plausible with 70+ stores and mail-in, but it still needs repair volume, turnaround, routing, and staffing data or the operations angle will sag.
gaps_in_B: "repair and resale programs are being expanded as described" invents a resale expansion. The update gives a repair expansion and a 500,000-item resale milestone, not a new resale rollout.
"right to repair" is dragged in as a beat without a supplied current peg. As written, it risks trend garnish.
"Patagonia opens free repairs at every US store" blurs an important qualifier: basic repairs are free; complex repairs are charged at cost.
The data angle and "The retailer that won't say how much money its sustainability story makes" both lean on the same revenue-disclosure gap, so the set is less distinct than it looks.
